source.title_on_document: ChatGPT como catalizador del pensamiento creativo [ChatGPT as a Catalyst for Creative Thinking]

supplement.where: The article refers to no supplementary material or online appendix.

paper_design_summary: All seventh-grade students (ages 12-13) at one science-humanities school in the O'Higgins region of Chile took the Torrance Test of Creative Thinking (verbal form A) before and after a classroom activity in which they wrote original songs with ChatGPT. There was no control group. The paper reports fluency, flexibility, originality, and a final/overall TTCT score and compares pretest and posttest with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

studies.label: Single-group pretest-posttest, ChatGPT song-writing intervention (TTCT verbal form A)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing was assigned at random. The whole seventh-grade population of one school (three courses, A, B, C) took part in the ChatGPT song-writing activity, and each student was tested before and after it. No control group.
assignment.quote: La investigación se llevó a cabo en un colegio científico-humanista ubicado en la región de O'Higgins, Chile, abarcando a toda la población de séptimo básico sin la implementación de un grupo de control.

arms.name: Pretest
arms.description: TTCT verbal form A taken before the ChatGPT song-writing activity (same students as the posttest)

arms.name: Posttest
arms.description: TTCT verbal form A taken after the song-writing activity with ChatGPT (same students as the pretest)

participants.who: Seventh-grade (séptimo básico) students aged 12-13 at one science-humanities school in the O'Higgins region, Chile; three courses (A, B, C). The paper does not explicitly report the number of students analyzed or the number of complete pretest-posttest pairs.
participants.quote: El estudio pretende evaluar los efectos del uso de la inteligencia artificial (ChatGPT) en el desarrollo del pensamiento creativo de estudiantes de entre 12 y 13 años.
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 2 (population and ages); p. 15, Section 3.5 (three courses); pp. 6-7, Sections 2-2.1 and p. 13, Tabla 3 (no explicit analyzed-person or complete-pair count)

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT (the paper describes it as based on GPT-3, p. 5)
ai_tool.how_used: Students created original songs using ChatGPT to generate ideas, develop the lyrics, and structure the text and harmonic progression; they were instructed on how to interact with the model and integrate its suggestions (p. 6, Section 2.1; p. 7).

task.description: Intervention task: collaborative creation of original song lyrics about common adolescent experiences with ChatGPT. Scored task: Torrance Test of Creative Thinking, verbal form A, before and after the intervention, scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality (elaboration not scored).

contrasts.reported: Posttest vs pretest (same students): Originalidad media 12,54 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 11,39-13,70; mediana 12,00) at pretest vs 14,21 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 12,96-15,47; mediana 13,50) at posttest. Wilcoxon signed-rank test for related samples: Sig. 0,000 (asymptotic, as printed), 'Rechace la hipótesis nula'. No SDs printed for this dimension.
contrasts.locator: p. 10, Gráfico 2 (descriptive table) and text; p. 13, Tabla 3

contrasts.reported: Posttest vs pretest (same students): Flexibilidad media 3,19 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 2,50-3,87; mediana 3,00) at pretest vs 4,31 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 3,51-5,12; mediana 4,00) at posttest. Wilcoxon signed-rank test for related samples: Sig. 0,000 (asymptotic, as printed), 'Rechace la hipótesis nula'. No SDs printed for this dimension.
contrasts.locator: p. 10, Gráfico 2 (descriptive table) and text; p. 13, Tabla 3

contrasts.reported: Posttest vs pretest (same students): Fluidez media 7,84 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 7,13-8,55; mediana 7,00) at pretest vs 7,77 (95% CI for the timepoint mean 6,75-8,79; mediana 7,00) at posttest. Wilcoxon signed-rank test for related samples: Sig. 0,517 (asymptotic, as printed), 'Conserve la hipótesis nula'. No SDs printed for this dimension.

outcomes.name: TTCT final/overall score (Final E and Final S)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: TTCT verbal form A final/overall score, labeled Final E at pretest and Final S at posttest. The article does not state how this score was constructed. Tablas 2-3 report descriptive timepoint statistics and a paired Wilcoxon test; the confidence intervals describe timepoint means, not the change (p. 8, Tabla 2; p. 13, Tabla 3).

contrasts.reported: Pretest (Final E): media 23,57 (SD 8,485; 95% CI for the timepoint mean 21,55-25,59; mediana 22,00); Posttest (Final S): media 26,30 (SD 11,395; 95% CI for the timepoint mean 23,58-29,02; mediana 24,00). Same participants at both timepoints. Related-samples Wilcoxon signed-rank test: Sig. 0,000 (asymptotic, as printed), 'Rechace la hipótesis nula'. These are descriptive timepoint statistics and a paired significance test; no standardized effect, paired-change SE, or confidence interval for the change is reported.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Tabla 2 and accompanying text; p. 13, Tabla 3, Final E/Final S row and footnote b

eligibility.reason: Single-group pretest-posttest: the school's seventh-grade population used ChatGPT without a control group, and no random assignment is described (p. 6, Sections 2-2.1), so criterion 1 is not met and core eligibility is no. Criterion 2 is unclear: the methods give no explicit analyzed-person count, and the gl values in the normality table are not an explicit count of analyzed participants or complete pairs (pp. 6-7, Sections 2-2.1; p. 8, Tabla 1; p. 13, Tabla 3). Criterion 3 is met by TTCT scores on students' verbal responses, with fluency, flexibility, originality, and final/overall scores reported (p. 6, Section 2; p. 8, Tabla 2; p. 10, Gráfico 2; p. 13, Tabla 3). Retain as observational context.

one_line_finding: In Chilean seventh graders tested before and after a ChatGPT song-writing activity (no control group), TTCT originality rose from 12.54 to 14.21 and flexibility from 3.19 to 4.31 (Wilcoxon Sig. 0.000 each), fluency showed no clear change (7.84 to 7.77, Sig. 0.517), and the final/overall score rose from 23.57 (SD 8.485) to 26.30 (SD 11.395) (pp. 8, 10, 13; Tablas 2-3, Gráfico 2).
notes: Tabla 1 prints gl = 70 for Final E and Final S in both the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests (p. 8). This is indirect sample-size evidence, not an explicit author-reported count of people analyzed or complete pairs, so it is not entered as participant n. The Pretest and Posttest entries describe timepoints for the same school population, not independent groups. The after_ai coding follows the TTCT posttest after the ChatGPT activity; the paper does not explicitly state whether AI was available during TTCT administration or the posttest delay (p. 6, Section 2.1). Blank AI-availability and timing fields reflect this lack of information. Confidence intervals are for individual timepoint means, not pretest-posttest changes; no paired-change SE or standardized effect is reported (pp. 8, 10 and 13).
